chunks: And that which was narrated is: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil and Muhammad ibn Humran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

Regarding a free man upon whom fasting two consecutive months is obligatory due to Dhahr, so he fasts one month then falls ill; he said: 'He resumes [the fast], and if he exceeds the other month by one or two days, he builds upon what remains [of the required two months].'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for expiation of Dhahr if the fasting is interrupted by illness?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia juristic view on the continuity (*mutatabi'*) of expiatory fasting for *Dhahr*, emphasizing that minor interruptions due to illness do not reset the count but rather extend the period. It highlights the principle of leniency in fulfilling religious obligations when hindered by valid excuses, ensuring the total duration of two lunar months is met without undue hardship. This ruling is crucial for distinguishing between a complete break in continuity and a temporary pause, reflecting the practical application of *fiqh* in personal status law.
